newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker Maritime considers listing on NYSE.
newsitem.headline: Aker Maritime considers listing on NYSE.

text.p: Norwegian offshore group Aker Maritime ASA said on Thursday it was considering whether to seek a listing on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in 1997.

"A stock exchange listing in the United States would bring increased liquidity to Aker Maritime's stock," a company statement said. "A number of companies in Aker Maritime's field are listed in the NYSE, and it is likely that over time its stock would be priced on par with these companies."

It added that considerations of a U.S. listing also reflected its ambitions for international expansion. A NYSE listing would enable Aker Maritime to be used in the pursuit of strategic mergers and acquisitions in North America and other international markets, it said.

Aker Maritime was formed last year after Aker ASA spun off its Oil and Gas Technology division and announced a merger with offshore supplier Maritime Group. Aker ASA later announced it would join forces with investment group Resource Group International ASA (RGI) to form Aker RGI ASA.
Both companies are listed on the Oslo bourse.

Aker Maritime said AKER RGI, which holds around 75 percent of the Maritime group's shares, had declared its intention of reducing its stake in the company and thus increasing the free flow of Aker Maritime stock in the market.
A spokesman for Aker RGI said the group was considering reducing its interest to under 70 percent.

The company said its board had not made a final decision on whether to seek an NYSE listing. U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley and Norwegian brokerage Orkla Finans have been appointed advisors to the company.
